questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university has some really niche and interesting courses that matches well with studying sociology.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite confusing for the first weeks to figure out the system and how to get the courses we wanted. But we heard from previously attending students that you just had to show up for the classes you wanted and then enroll later.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a personal check in, we did it online and received some information through there. Other than that i don't recall us getting any information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We found housing through an agent. Very expensive but easy. we only chose this option because we were four people who wanted to live together and couldn't find that big of an appartment on our own. If i was travelling alone i would probably recommend finding a room through facebook as it is way cheaper. And the city is small and walkable so living outside of the city walls is no problem.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't think it is an option at all to live on campus. But get a cheap bike! The campusses are all over town and often you have to rush from one class to another back to back.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again our appartment was really nice but very expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again, at first it was complicated but the actual system was very straight forward and UniBos online platform is very easy to use. Everything surrounding enrollment and course registration is done through there or by sending the professor an email.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Same as above.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: emailing the professors is the best way to get help i would say.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses i applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be strategic with you courses and plan ahead a time schedule and ects points. It thought it was very stressful trying to match up the courses and make a schedule that fit with 30 ects and was manageable both with exams and time schedules.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of the courses dont really have reading that you need to do so it can be kind of hard to follow what is going on at times and what the focus of the lecture will be beforhand.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A lot of the courses that fit my interests were MA courses. it was completely fine to follow even though they were above my level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different from UCPH and way more relaxed and personal.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Political Ecology of Work, Atlantic and Global History of Modern Political Concepts, Geography and Cognition of
European Territories, Introduction to Italian Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Geography and Cognition of European Territories. Very cool teacher and a completely new way of thinking space and geography!

questions.answer: We had to put down a large deposit for our appartment.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Train to other cities could sometimes be very expensive. so if you want to take the train around italy book tickets in good time in advance!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Bologna has a million things to do and a lot of events. I am however not sure what they provide through the school but the city it self has loads of opportunities and events.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going hiking in the mountains! join the outdoor whatsapp groups and find people to hike with through there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to Rome, Venice, Modena - Cities reachable by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Northern italy is very easy to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak with the students in class:)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Cant really think of anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: bolognas very potent political and activist scene. Both the students and teachers were very engaged in activistic activities and frequently demonstrated or made school lockdowns in solidarity with Palestine. It was a very inspiring energy to be around.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Everything is very relaxed so don't stress:)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The exam grading system is very generous, so don't worry about failing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having a semester only with courses i had choosen for myself and the nice and slow tempo of italy.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Can't really think of anything.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No i dont think so.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
